GENERAL THETA FOUNDATIONS I:
         ACQUIRED GEOMETRY AND CAUSAL RESOURCE TRANSFER

                                                      QIAN QI


        Abstract. We study the exact classical memory required to reproduce the laws of a causal
        experiment. For compactly reversible finite-dimensional responses, every finite stochastic realization
        reduces to a permutation core and at most one counted initializer. We prove that, for every finite
        observable group, sufficiently small positive terminal contrast makes the least core equal to the least
        dimension of a permutation module containing the observable module. All memory thresholds along
        the contrast line are attained. For groups whose subgroups are all normal, an absorption theorem
        reduces the exact optimization to quotient linear programs with explicit payoff duals and rational

GENERAL THETA FOUNDATIONS I:
         ACQUIRED GEOMETRY AND CAUSAL RESOURCE TRANSFER

                                                     QIAN QI


        Abstract. We study finite-resource prediction in positive prepared causal experiments using
        an actually prepared comparison law that need not belong to the operating model family. A
        reference-side converse replaces only each productive report–audit row while retaining the actual
        pre-call occupation. The resulting positive submeasure has controlled missing mass, a cost-certified
        density cap and controlled task moments, giving a lower bound uniform over all legal strategies.
        A common parameter-independent approximate balancing program gives a matching upper at the
        same expected physical budget. The bounds recover exact stopped risk profiles at zero error and
        matching acquired-geometry orders on a quantified two-sided calibration regime. Drift certificates
        extend the converse to metastable and singular calibration with explicit preparation mass and

GENERAL THETA FOUNDATIONS I:
                            CURRENT TECHNICAL SUPPLEMENT

                                                      QIAN QI


        Abstract. This is the current technical companion to the theorem article. It supplies the inherited
        sharp four-period transition, followed by the recurrent-projection proof for the reversible normal form
        and the complete periodic, arithmetic, spectral and leakage arguments. The complete causal synthesis,
        performed-law, compact-model, minimax, dual, stopping, finite-width, reset, discrimination, acquired-
        geometry and realization proofs remain included, together with preparation faces, legality, deadlock,
        continuation and audit compilation. Each statement retains its individual hypotheses; the new
        positive-realization results do not replace the independent optimization or Theta construction
        problems.



References to the main article use ordinary section numbers; statements numbered S belong to this
supplement. Both native documents are compiled together. The main article contains complete
proofs of the general contrast, quotient-dual and conditional-memory results, the reversible criterion
and normal form, algebraic synthesis, finite certificates and actual-history comparison. The theorem
map gives the exact native source, number and page for every current statement.
